title: Harden streaming client: robust SSE parsing, cancellation semantics, and tests for partial frames/disconnects
author: Ibrahim Khan
release_notes: Python SDK: improved streaming robustness (SSE parsing across partial frames, consistent cancellation behavior). Adds tests covering mid-stream disconnects and proxy-style chunking. No API surface changes; behavior is more deterministic on disconnect/cancel.
description: Context: We’ve had multiple reports of streaming “hangs” and inconsistent errors when clients sit behind proxies that buffer/chunk responses unpredictably (SUP-9321). This PR hardens SSE parsing to handle partial frames and split boundaries, makes cancellation semantics deterministic, and adds regression tests for disconnect edge cases. This is intended to align with the cross-SDK streaming semantics work (ENG-2483) while keeping Python behavior stable and observable. What changed: (1) SSE parser: treat the response as an arbitrary byte stream; accumulate until full event boundaries are available; tolerate split "data:" lines and split "\n\n" terminators across chunks; ignore empty keepalive frames and leading BOM; enforce a max buffered event size to avoid unbounded memory growth; surface malformed events with a structured StreamingParseError that includes a safe preview (redacted) and byte offsets. (2) Disconnect handling: if the socket drops mid-event, we now raise StreamingDisconnectError with fields: bytes_read, events_emitted, request_id (if available), and an explicit guidance string (“do not automatically retry streaming requests; caller may retry non-streaming with idempotency key”). If disconnect happens after a fully emitted event boundary, we don’t retroactively error; we exit only when we fail to read the next frame. (3) Cancellation: when the user cancels iteration (GeneratorExit / task cancel) or calls close(), we now (a) close the underlying response body, (b) stop background read tasks, and (c) raise a consistent StreamCancelledError only if the caller is actively iterating and the cancellation is external; normal loop break does not turn into an exception. Async client uses asyncio.CancelledError mapping; sync client maps KeyboardInterrupt separately and ensures connection cleanup. (4) Tests: added deterministic tests that simulate partial frames, proxy-style chunk sizes, and mid-stream disconnects. Added a fuzz-style test that randomizes chunk boundaries for a fixed SSE transcript. Added tests to ensure request-id propagation into errors when present. Non-goals: automatic reconnect/resume for streaming; server-side changes; changing the public streaming API shape. Checklist: - [x] Added unit tests for partial framing and disconnects - [x] Verified cancellation closes the HTTP response (no file descriptor leaks) - [x] Error messages avoid including secrets / headers - [x] Docsstrings updated for streaming error taxonomy (brief; fuller docs in docs PR) Notes for reviewers: The parser changes are intentionally conservative and preserve existing emitted event payloads. The primary behavior change is that some previously “silent hangs” now terminate with a StreamingDisconnectError when the transport ends mid-event, which is preferable for production.

notable_snippets: SSE parsing now accumulates bytes until a full event delimiter (\n\n) is present; "data:" lines can be split across reads without losing content.
On disconnect mid-event: raise StreamingDisconnectError(events_emitted=n, bytes_read=m, request_id=..., message="Stream disconnected mid-event; do not auto-retry streaming.")
Cancellation ensures response.close() is called in finally blocks for both sync and async iterators.
review_conversation: Amara Diallo (gateway): Do we have a consistent rule for whether to include request-id in these errors? Some proxies drop headers on disconnect.

Ibrahim Khan (author): If we have it from initial response headers we thread it into the stream context; if the connection drops later we still have the last known request-id. If we never received headers (rare) it will be None. Tests cover both cases.
Rafael Mendes (SRE): Please confirm we’re not adding any automatic retries for streaming; we don’t want retry amplification for long-lived streams.

Ibrahim Khan (author): Confirmed. No reconnect/resume logic; on disconnect we surface StreamingDisconnectError. Retry guidance is text-only in the error message; actual retry policies live in the retry standard PRs.
Monica Patel (DevEx): The new StreamCancelledError behavior—will it break existing callers who currently catch generic Exception on cancel?

Ibrahim Khan (author): It should be safer: we only raise StreamCancelledError when cancellation is external while actively iterating. If the user simply breaks out of the loop, we just close and return. This avoids surprising exceptions on normal loop termination.
Sahana Iyer (CI/conformance): CI failed once with a flaky timing assertion in async disconnect test—can we remove reliance on sleep?
Ibrahim Khan (author): Updated the async test to use a deterministic fake transport and an explicit "disconnect" signal; removed sleeps. Re-ran CI and it’s stable.
requested_changes: Tighten the async disconnect test to avoid timing-based flakiness (remove sleeps).
Cap buffered event size and add a targeted test for oversized events.
Make sure error previews redact non-UTF8 bytes safely (avoid decode explosions).
